name: Chewing gum for face fat

lead: Some appearance forums say chewing gum for long stretches slims the cheeks and sharpens the jawline by working the jaw muscles and burning facial fat.

The idea is a version of spot reduction. Exercise research cited in encyclopedic sources reports that fat is lost from the whole body through overall energy balance, with distribution largely set by genetics, rather than from the exercised site. No published human trial found has tested chewing gum for facial fat. Gum has been studied for other outcomes, including short-term memory, dental plaque and bowel recovery after abdominal surgery.

paras: People chew sugar-free gum for extended periods each day, often alongside diet changes and other jaw routines, and judge results by looking in the mirror over weeks.
Gum is generally regarded as low risk. Sorbitol-sweetened gum in large amounts may cause gas or diarrhea.

angle.text: Appearance forum users chew gum hoping to work the cheek muscles and slim the face. The idea is that chewing burns fat locally, a spot-reduction approach that exercise research does not support. No trial has tested gum for facial fat.

lead: Chewing gum for face fat is a practice, found in appearance-focused online communities, of chewing gum for long stretches to slim the cheeks and sharpen the jawline. Practitioners say the repeated jaw work burns fat over the cheeks and jaw or builds the chewing muscles, so that the lower face looks leaner and more defined.[1][2]

The idea belongs to the family of facial-slimming ideas built on spot reduction, the principle that exercising one muscle group reduces fat in the area around it. Encyclopedic sources describe spot reduction and report exercise studies finding that fat is lost from the whole body through diet and overall energy balance rather than from the exercised site.[3] A T Nation forum poster in 2002 made the same point in lay terms: chewing lots of gum does not make the face 'ripped'.[4]

No published human trial found has tested chewing gum for facial fat.[5] Chewing gum has been studied for other outcomes, including short-term memory, dental plaque and recovery of bowel function after abdominal surgery.[5]

paras: Proponents of the practice say that extended chewing works the jaw and cheek muscles and thereby thins the face or sharpens the jawline. Variations include chewing for long sessions each day and using hard or mastic-style gums.
The practice is closely related to jaw-exerciser devices and to arguments about masseter size, but this article concerns gum itself.

sections.h: Use in looksmaxxing and fitness communities
paras: A 2003 T Nation thread on training jaw muscles included a poster saying everyone he knew with strong jaw muscles chewed gum constantly, and adding that low body fat helps because the face loses fat quickly and features show more.[1] A 2002 thread on spot reduction included a reply that targeted muscle work does not reduce fat locally, citing chewing gum and the face as an example.[4] A T Nation article on eating habits, titled 'Strong Jaw, Lean Body', discusses how eating speed and chewing relate to the face and appetite.[2]

Many in these communities distinguish two effects: muscle growth in the jaw, which they argue could add width and definition, and fat loss over the cheeks, which they attribute mainly to lowering overall body fat.

Spot reduction is described as a claim that physiologists and fitness professionals regard as unsupported by research. In a six-week trial of 24 sedentary adults cited in the encyclopedic literature, a group performing abdominal exercises five days a week did not lose subcutaneous abdominal fat, although core endurance improved.[3] A study of tennis players cited there found larger muscles in the dominant forearm but no difference in skinfold fat between arms.[3]

The same source states that fat distribution is strongly influenced by genetics and that fat is lost from the body as a whole through diet and regular exercise.[3] These findings concern the trunk and limbs; the sources reviewed here do not report trials of facial fat in particular.

sections.h: Other documented effects of chewing gum
paras: A 2011 review found that chewing gum before cognitive testing was associated with better working and episodic memory for roughly 15 to 20 minutes.[5] Sugar-free gum sweetened with xylitol has been shown to reduce cavities and plaque, and the American Dental Association recommends chewing sugar-free gum for 20 minutes after meals.[5] Randomized studies and a 2008 meta-analysis reported faster bowel recovery after colectomy in patients who chewed gum.[5]

Gum containing sorbitol in large amounts may cause gas or diarrhea, and a 2025 study reported that gum releases micro- and nanoplastics into saliva; the health effects of this are under investigation.[5] None of these outcomes concern facial appearance.

No studies found. No published trial in the sources reviewed has measured changes in facial fat after gum chewing. Related research on spot reduction in the abdomen and forearm is summarised above.[3]

lore.intro: Chewing is discussed in strength-training and appearance forums as a way to build the jaw and lean the face, with other posters pointing to overall body fat as the main driver.[1][4]
